extracted.intended_audience: aspiring theatre critics, students of arts criticism, and general readers interested in theatre review/criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the distinguishing purposes, audiences, timing, scope, and analytical depth of theatre reviews versus theatre criticism — what to cover, when to publish, and how deeply to analyse a production. Useful for writers deciding whether to produce a review (timely, reader-facing) or a piece of criticism (scholarly, contextual).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: theatre criticism vs drama criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatre criticism is a critique of the theatrical performance, whereas drama criticism is a division of literary criticism; dramas remain literature in print but become part of the performing arts when staged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the appropriate critical approach depending on whether you are evaluating the written play (literary/drama criticism) or the staged performance (theatre criticism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review: purpose and target audience
rubrics_metrics.description: A theatre review is a short essay for the ordinary uninitiated readers who get to know about the play being performed, about the group staging the play, and its director and other actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are a subjective discourse that hint at the cultural and artistic significance of the production and reflect an instant reaction of viewing the performance. They should be accessible to general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review: focus on storyline and immediate reaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The storyline is discussed as it is believed to be the mainstay of the production; the discussion reflects an instant reaction of viewing the performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise plot and immediate impressions rather than deep theoretical analysis when writing a review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review: coverage of production departments
rubrics_metrics.description: A review includes an overall clinical analysis of each department of the production, like that of acting, stage craft, lighting designs and its implementation, background scoring, dress and costume designing, make-up etc., and even the script prepared for staging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Touch on the major practical components of the production so readers understand strengths/weaknesses across departments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review: timing and speed of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A review is published during the period when the play is 'on', that is, when the play is being regularly staged. This requires a speedy writing of the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of the need for speed and timeliness, reviews generally lack deep analytical discourse and do not give conclusive verdicts about the production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism: depth and analytical scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Theatre criticism is a deep analytical discourse of the production against the backdrop of the theatre-arts as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism is more theoretical and objective, functioning like an academic dissertation; it is lengthy and may take considerable time to write.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism: contextualization of social, political, and cultural bearings
rubrics_metrics.description: The social and political bearings that have relevance to the play are highlighted, so also the cultural import; hence the discussion becomes a highly theoretical objective discourse on the historical significance of the production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate the production within broader social, political, and cultural contexts and explore its historical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism: technical and exhaustive departmental analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Technicalities of the different aspects of the production are discussed in details together with exhaustive analysis of the rationalities of their execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide in-depth examination of why design/acting/directorial choices were made and how effectively they were executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism: timing and permanence
rubrics_metrics.description: A piece of criticism may be published even after the regular staging of the play has been suspended or stopped, or a subsequent production of a different play has been started by the group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism does not need to be tied to the run dates; it can be retrospective and benefit from additional research and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role boundary: theatrical vs literary focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism is an anatomical scrutiny of the production; the play is not discussed in detail as such, as it is job of the literary critic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing theatre criticism, focus on the performance and production elements rather than re-analyzing the play-as-text, which is the domain of literary critics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: philosophical/political/moral criticism may be anti-theatrical
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophical, political or moral criticism may be considered anti-theatrical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that certain modes of criticism (explicitly moralizing or political) can be perceived as hostile to theatrical practice; weigh such approaches accordingly.
